cards.note: repository-plugins mechanism: the tree ships no dsh.plugin.json and no repository rows; it already declares dsh.bundle.patch (package.json:11-15) and mounts through the profile bundle list, which is the recipe's target state.
No dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json anywhere in the tree; the plugin has no client half to declare.
Host-only plugin (no dsh.client, no client bundle), so the client-modules scan contract does not consider it.

The one host service the plugin consumes (llm) is declared in inject and read through the declared property; there is no ctx.get/undeclared access, and the target cold boot activates the row instead of leaving it pending.
llm is a mandatory dependency of this activation probe and is provided by the dsh-base layer every documented profile starts from; there is no optional host service to probe weakly.
No session/event subscription and no session-state derivation in the plugin.
No Web Client half; the plugin runs only in the host plane and has no client-side session reads to move.
No tasks/jobs output tailing; the plugin never called tasks.peek.
No httpServer/webServer, tasks/jobs or onTaskDone/onJobDone usage anywhere in the tree; its only service is llm.
No ImageAttachmentRef, read_image or image metadata in the plugin.
The plugin neither registers, wraps, parses nor snapshots read_image output.
No LLM adapter, image request interceptor or attachment/upload cache in the plugin.

The legacy ctx.apiProxy.llm.providers() call was the only APIProxy hit; it now uses the owning host-plane service (inject llm + ctx.llm.listProviders()) and the dead @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy dependency is gone; the target boot reaches the model call.
The plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents, and the target alpha.2 is past the alpha.1-only removal (A2-01 restored the field), so nothing is deleted or re-added.
No host-source patches and no imports from internal session-view paths.
The plugin contributes a bundle patch, it does not read profile files; no launcher wrapper, Python SDK/ACP integration or demo bin.
The plugin writes its own [upgrade-demo] lines to stderr; it neither parses host stdout/stderr nor emits the dsh: reasoning: segment.
No tool-presentation mode, PTC preset or dispatch waterfall usage.
Not a permission/approval/WebFetch policy plugin and owns no preset rows.
No custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC, browser page or /api route in the plugin.
Optional capability; the plugin is not a model-provider plugin and carries no settings-page patch or shim for it to retire.
Optional capability; no localization resources or custom i18n patch in the plugin.
Optional capability; no subagent orchestration or provider/model selector in the plugin.
Informational privacy card for deployments using the official DeepSeek adapter; plugin code does not touch package-name attribution.
No persistent-PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker workaround to retire.
Optional privacy capability; the plugin has no session-log egress configuration (the boot probe sets DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED only in the check harness).
No browser acceptance script or web-root URL handling; the documented verification path is a headless profile boot, not dsh web.
No userQuestions answerer registration.
No agent-preset inference or agent-presets roots usage.
Does not import isTokenDelta or compute tokens-per-second.
The plugin contributes one insert row and maintains no profile/dsh-base composition, so it has no telemetry or package-inventory stance to restate.
No @earendil-works/pi-ai import and no provider/auth plugin surface.
No @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime imports, no dsh.client.inject.
No Web Client half, so the three-id scan contract does not apply; the host assembly row already names the bare package (@demo/dsh-upgrade-demo) in cordis.patch.yml:3.
No session timeline or user-message content reads.
No composer DOM manipulation (draft injection, history recall or selection).
No MarkdownText/CodeBlock rendering from ui-primitives.
No client ctx.connection.api usage or history/transcript reads.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptors.
No ctx.workspaces/ctx.uiWorkspace navigation or directory-picker calls.
The plugin writes no third-party persisted SessionEvents, so the alpha.2 restore has no producer-side effect here.
The probe uses the host-plane llm service (plain array), not ctx.remote/RemoteResult/RemoteError.
The plugin declares no peers and imports nothing; its only dependency edge (the dead apiproxy package) is removed under A1-01, not a peer-trim action.
No dsh web startup wrapper or Node-version workaround; the check runs Node v24.21.0, outside the fixed 24.0-24.11.1 window.
The plugin does not consume pluginInventory/list or validate its snapshot.
No client Remote, no $host.home/isLoopback reads.
The plugin mounts none of the tool/agent packages that gained the sessionProjections peer; its composition is a single host row.
No ctx.settings register/update/get usage, so the compile-time namespace literal rule does not touch the plugin.
